result.Method of Attack: InfoStealer malware written in Python with paid customizations, steals sensitive information such as passwords, credit cards, cookies, session data, and keylogging from Windows hosts; collects system information, clipboard images, WLAN profiles, and screenshots; exfiltrates data via Discord webhook to threat actor-controlled channel
result.Attack Vector: Delivered via phishing, watering holes, or other malware (exact initial vector unknown); uses a decoy document (PDF) and a PyInstaller executable masquerading as 'Runtime Broker' to deploy malware
Indicators of Compromise: Telegram channel for purchase and GitHub repo for open-source version
Malware detected by Fortinet AV signatures: W32/ExelaStealer.0943!tr, W32/ExelaStealer.C93A!tr
